did_you_know.text: Did you know? The title “A Maskil of Asaph” indicates that this is an instructional psalm attributed to Asaph. It opens with a call to listen to the teaching and the words spoken.

Did you know? The psalm presents the teaching and testimony as an intergenerational responsibility: the fathers are commanded to make the words of the LORD known to their children so that the tradition will continue for generations to come.
Did you know? The purpose of remembering history in the psalm is not merely to know the past, but also to inspire trust in God, remember his deeds, and keep his commandments.

Did you know? The descendants of Ephraim are described as warriors armed with bows, yet they turned back on the day of battle. The verse presents them as an example of a generation that failed to remain faithful.
Did you know? Israel’s journey through the wilderness is described as being guided in two ways: by a pillar of cloud by day and by the light of fire throughout the night.
Did you know? After the people question whether God can set a table in the wilderness, the psalm describes him opening the “doors of heaven” and sending down manna as food from heaven.
Did you know? Alongside the manna, the quail are also described: an east wind brings large numbers of birds, and they fall within the camp of Israel, around its dwellings.

Did you know? Amid its description of sin and punishment, the psalm emphasizes the LORD’s mercy: he forgives iniquity, repeatedly turns away his anger, and remembers that human beings are flesh and a passing breath.

Did you know? After Israel’s rebellion in the land, the psalm describes the abandonment of the sanctuary at Shiloh—the central sanctuary at that time—and the handing over of the people, his strength, and his glory to the enemy.

Did you know? At the end of the psalm, the focus of leadership changes: the LORD rejects the tent of Joseph and the tribe of Ephraim, chooses Judah and Zion, and finally brings David from tending the sheep to lead Israel with integrity and wisdom.
